title: Amazon and Google Win Big From Anthropic IPO
summary: If you’re looking for a cheaper way of getting exposure to Anthropic than buying the stock directly, consider Amazon or Google. Anthropic’s updated IPO filing on Tuesday shows just how many shares each of those two tech giants will own in Anthropic, along with how much money they’re making on their early investments in the AI firm.Neither tech giant will own voting shares in Anthropic, so antitrust cops won’t have to worry about their influence over its management. But their stakes are significant. In theory, Amazon could own around 20% of Anthropic’s outstanding shares. But because of a self-imposed ownership cap, Amazon won’t hold more than 12% of Anthropic. The rest of its holdings are convertible notes that can convert to equity over time. Regardless, Amazon’s economic return is pretty damn good. Forgetting about the ownership cap for a minute, Amazon’s entire 20%-or-so stake would be worth about $258 billion at the midpoint of Anthropic’s proposed IPO pricing range. That’s from an investment totaling around $18.6 billion. (Anthropic’s final IPO price may well end up higher than the preliminary range,a Financial Times reporttonight suggests).
title_es: Amazon y Google multiplican inversión en Anthropic con su IPO
bajada: Amazon y Google obtendrán ganancias masivas de sus inversiones tempranas en Anthropic tras su salida a bolsa. Amazon podría ver su inversión de $18.6 mil millones convertirse en $258 mil millones, aunque se autoimpone un límite de participación del 12% para evitar problemas antimonopolio.
bajada_en: Amazon and Google will see massive returns on their early Anthropic investments following the company's IPO. Amazon's $18.6 billion investment could be worth around $258 billion at the midpoint of the IPO pricing, though it self-imposes a 12% ownership cap to avoid antitrust concerns.

title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
summary:
arXiv:2611.12933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. Provenance showed that 59-68% of error corrections involved multiple participants and that about half of all decisions incorporated the input of another participant. These results may guide design principles for multi-agent scientific systems and inform future agent harnesses, model training, and accessible autonomous experimentation.
title_es: Agentes audibles para experimentos autónomos de rayos X sincrotrónico
bajada: Investigadores demostraron sistemas humano-agente auditable que ejecutan experimentos de rayos X sincrotrónico autónomos con transparencia total sobre decisiones. Este trabajo establece principios de diseño para sistemas multi-agente científicos confiables y verificables.
bajada_en: Researchers demonstrated auditable human-agent systems that execute autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments with complete decision transparency. This work establishes design principles for trustworthy and verifiable multi-agent scientific systems.

title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
summary:
arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.
title_es: EarthRecord: agentes multimodales analizan cuatro décadas de satélites
bajada: Se introduce EarthRecord, un benchmark que evalúa agentes multimodales procesando 56 sitios de datos satelitales sin procesar de cuatro décadas para análisis de cambios de tierra. Este benchmark revela limitaciones actuales de agentes IA en tareas de análisis geoespacial complejas.
bajada_en: EarthRecord introduces a benchmark evaluating multimodal agents processing raw satellite data from four decades across 56 sites for land-change analysis. This benchmark reveals current limitations of AI agents in complex geospatial analysis tasks.
